**Stability fixes for saving, separate audio tracks, monitor switching and shutdown.**

**Download:** `ClipRing-v0.2.1-win-x64.zip` below, unzip, start `ClipRing.exe`. No installation; .NET and FFmpeg are included. Your settings are kept.

### Fixed
- **File names:** custom templates that resolve to reserved Windows names (such as `CON`), trailing dots or only punctuation are now sanitized safely instead of producing invalid names.
- **Monitor switching and locked screens:** switching to another monitor now applies the remembered mode profile (and frame-rate limit), and locked or sleeping displays no longer trigger repeated "Monitor mode changed" notifications and restarts.
- **Separate audio tracks:** toggling the option when only one audio source is active no longer restarts and clears the buffer, memory estimates now account for all three audio tracks, and audio pipe diagnostics report the actual channel rate.
- **Startup and shutdown reliability:** changing settings during startup detection can no longer race with encoder/monitor probing, quitting cancels in-flight probes cleanly, and cancelling a clip remux stops its FFmpeg process right away.
- **Live status & UI details:** changing buffer length or the save hotkey now updates the overview status line immediately, file sizes and estimated bitrates follow the selected app language, Epic and GOG paths with forward slashes match properly, and opening an unreachable clip folder no longer raises an unhandled error.

### Under the hood
- Thread-safety hardening for monitor mode profiles (copy-on-write during settings saves), `ReplayRecorder` frame-rate tracking, audio pipe buffer cleanup, and device watch reads.
- Expanded unit tests covering file-name templates, pipeline arguments, encoder fallbacks, localization parity and `known_games.json`.

Windows may warn because the program is not signed yet: click **More info → Run anyway**.
